newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mt Kare results Porgera-like - Carpenter.
newsitem.headline: Mt Kare results Porgera-like - Carpenter.

text.p: Gold explorer Carpenter Pacific Resources NL said on Friday that the latest drilling results from its Mout Kare gold project in Papua New Guinea confirmed that the deposit was similar to the nearby Porgera gold mine.
Carpenter said assay results showed gold of up to a massive 2,140.98 grams per tonne (g/t) and as low as 0.62 g/t.

"The results reinforce the company's confidence that Mount Kare is a very significant gold asset, exhibiting the same gold mineralisation structure and character as the 24-million ounce gold resource at the producing Porgera gold mine," it said.
Porgera is 15 kms to the northeast of Mount Kare.
The drilling carried out by Mount Kare joint venture partner Madison Enterprises Corp of Canada was the first significant drilling taken out at the prospect since 1990.
Carpenter said the results reaffirm the initial excellent grades identified by former Mount Kare licence holder, RTZ-CRA, in its 32-hole drilling program across Mount Kare in the late 1980s.

"The various styles of mineralisation identified at both Porgera and Mt Kare are very similar in geologic setting, age, mineralization and structural controls," Madison Enterprises said in a statement issued with Carpenter's statement.
"Madison's geologic model and exploration target at Mt Kare is the discovery and delineation of a Porgera-style gold deposit," Madison said.

Madison said the drilling programme was planned to continue through to 1998 on a regular grid pattern on the Main Zone and its extensions, and other targets such as the Northeast and North Zones as they are developed during the exploration work.
At 3.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), Carpenter shares were 10.5 cents up at 29 cents with over 9.7 million shares traded.
